# Markov assumptions and the Poisson equation {#sec-assumptions}

The central obstacle is not the algebra of PCA but the fact that the same Markov chain is used to update its own transition kernel.  The estimates below use weighted norms in the sense of @andrieuMoulines2006, Section 3, and its common-invariant-distribution framework.

## Target and kernel conditions

::: {#asm-target-M}
## Andrieu--Moulines condition (M)

The target density $\pi$ on $\mathbb R^d$ is bounded, continuously differentiable and bounded away from zero on every compact subset.  It satisfies

$$
\lim_{\|x\|\to\infty}
\left\langle \frac{x}{\|x\|},\nabla\log\pi(x)\right\rangle=-\infty
$$ {#eq-condition-M-tails}

and

$$
\limsup_{\|x\|\to\infty}
\left\langle \frac{x}{\|x\|},
\frac{\nabla\pi(x)}{\|\nabla\pi(x)\|}\right\rangle<0.
$$ {#eq-condition-M-contours}
:::

These super-exponential tail and contour conditions are sufficient, not necessary, conditions for the random-walk Metropolis estimates used here.  They imply that all polynomial moments of $\pi$ exist; the strictly positive density implies the target covariance $C$ is positive definite.  Following A&M, choose

$$
V(x)=\pi(x)^{-\eta}/(\sup_y\pi(y))^{-\eta},
\qquad 0<\eta<1,
$$ {#eq-drift-weight}

so $V\geq1$.  For a vector- or matrix-valued observable $f$, use $\|f\|_{V^a}=\sup_x\|f(x)\|/V^a(x)$.

::: {#asm-kernel}
## Locally uniform Markov kernel control

For every compact $K\subset\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb S_{++}^d$, the family $P_\Gamma$, $(\mu,\Gamma)\in K$, satisfies uniform minorization and geometric drift with weight $V$, and the weighted operator bound

$$
\|(P_\Gamma-P_{\Gamma'})f\|_{V^a}
\leq L_{K,a}\|\Gamma-\Gamma'\|_F\|f\|_{V^a},
\qquad 0\leq a\leq1.
$$ {#eq-weighted-kernel-lipschitz}

Every $P_\Gamma$ preserves the same $\pi$.
:::

Proposition 12 and Lemma 13 of @andrieuMoulines2006 establish precisely these ingredients for the symmetric Gaussian random-walk Metropolis family under @asm-target-M.  Notice that $P_{\mu,\Gamma,W}=P_\Gamma$: adjoining $W$ adds **no new kernel dependence**.  Compactness of $\mathrm{St}(d,r)$ makes the constants uniform in $W$.

For a chain stopped when $(\mu_n,\Gamma_n)$ exits a compact parameter region, the drift bound yields a localized moment estimate of the form

$$
\sup_{n\geq0}\mathbb E[
V(X_n)\mathbf1_{\{\tau_K\geq n\}}]<\infty.
$$ {#eq-localized-moments}

This is the input used repeatedly in the summation arguments.

::: {#asm-step-sizes}
## Step sizes

The deterministic sequence $(\gamma_n)$ is nonincreasing, $0<\gamma_n<1$, and

$$
\sum_{n=1}^\infty\gamma_n=\infty,\qquad
\sum_{n=1}^\infty\gamma_n^2<\infty.
$$ {#eq-stepsizes}
:::

## Regularity of the full observable

::: {#lem-observable-regularity}
## Polynomial and weighted Lipschitz bounds

For every compact $K$ in the mean--covariance parameter domain, a constant $A_K$ exists such that for all $\theta,\theta'\in K\times\mathrm{St}(d,r)$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\|H(\theta,x)\|&\leq A_K(1+\|x\|^2),\\
\|H(\theta,x)-H(\theta',x)\|
&\leq A_K(1+\|x\|^2)\|\theta-\theta'\|.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-polynomial-regularity}

For the weight @eq-drift-weight, $H$ is locally $V^\beta$-Lipschitz for any fixed $0<\beta\leq1/2$.
:::

::: {.proof}
Write $z=x-\mu$, $z'=x-\mu'$.  From $\|W\|_{\mathrm{op}}=1$ and $\|I-WW^\top\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq1$,

$$
\|(I-WW^\top)zz^\top W\|_F\leq\|z\|^2.
$$

For parameter differences, use

$$
zz^\top-z'z'^\top=(z-z')z^\top+z'(z-z')^\top,
$$

together with $\|WW^\top-W'W'^\top\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq2\|W-W'\|_F$.  Add and subtract terms with $\mu'$ and $W'$ one at a time.  Because $\mu,\mu'$ are bounded on $K$, every difference is bounded by $A_K(1+\|x\|^2)\|\theta-\theta'\|$.  The first two coordinates of $H$ are simpler.  Under (M), $V^\beta$ dominates each fixed polynomial, so the weighted statements follow.
:::

## Poisson equation and its parameter regularity

Put $f_\theta(x)=H(\theta,x)-h(\theta)$.  The relevant Poisson solution is **Euclidean-valued**, not manifold-valued:

$$
u_\theta-P_\theta u_\theta=f_\theta,\qquad
u_\theta=\sum_{j=0}^\infty(P_\theta^jH_\theta-\pi H_\theta).
$$ {#eq-poisson}

Existence alone is not enough: changing $\theta$ generates differences of $P_\theta u_\theta$, which must be controlled.

::: {#lem-poisson-regularity}
## Uniform bounds and Lipschitz regularity

On every compact $K\times\mathrm{St}(d,r)$, there exists $L_K$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}
\|u_\theta\|_{V^\beta}+
  \|P_\theta u_\theta\|_{V^\beta}&\leq L_K,\\
\|u_\theta-u_{\theta'}\|_{V^\beta}
+\|P_\theta u_\theta-P_{\theta'}u_{\theta'}\|_{V^\beta}
&\leq L_K\|\theta-\theta'\|.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-poisson-lipschitz}
:::

::: {.proof}
Apply Proposition 3, equations (18)--(19), of @andrieuMoulines2006 to each coordinate of $f_\theta$, using @asm-kernel and @lem-observable-regularity.  The common invariant law and weighted geometric ergodicity ensure convergence of the Poisson series.  The operator regularity A2 is used for the Lipschitz estimate, as is explicit in A&M's appendix proof.  As the observable takes values in a fixed finite-dimensional ambient space, coordinatewise estimates suffice.
:::
